transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support. My name is Dominic. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Dominic. My home broadband keeps dropping connection completely every time someone uses the microwave in our kitchen. I already unscrewed the master phone socket faceplate and replaced the microfilter yesterday with a brand new S-Net filter, so the filter is definitely not the cause.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly investigate those intermittent broadband drops with you, Wendy. Before we inspect line telemetry, may I please verify your billing address and your security question answer?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 42 Highfield Road, Canterbury, CT1 3TG. And my security question answer is my mother's maiden name, Fletcher.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Wendy, that verifies your account. How often does this disconnect occur during the day?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It happens three or four times every single lunchtime! I am an NHS medical transcriptionist working on emergency cancer pathology reports with strict hospital deadlines! If the connection drops during my secure upload session, the whole batch corrupts and puts urgent patient treatments at severe risk! I am under extreme stress!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us check your router's wireless transmission logs and line sync history on our network monitor.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay... but please hurry, I have a batch due at one o'clock.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So if I have understood correctly, your internet connection cuts out whenever the kitchen microwave oven operates, disrupting your medical file transmissions, and you need the wireless interference resolved so your work can proceed reliably. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. Whenever the microwave runs for even thirty seconds to reheat soup, the WiFi icon on my laptop drops to zero bars.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am examining the Openreach copper loop test between our Canterbury telephone exchange and your master socket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does the line test show on the physical wire?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The copper VDSL sync at your master socket shows a continuous uptime of six days at thirty-eight megabits per second, with zero line drops or DSL retraining events.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, so the actual broadband cable from the street is not disconnecting?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is correct. The physical broadband link remains completely stable; what is failing is the local 2.4 gigahertz radio link between your router and laptop.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How can a microwave oven affect the WiFi signal across the hallway?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Domestic microwave ovens generate electromagnetic radiation at approximately 2.45 gigahertz, which sits squarely on top of standard WiFi channel 6.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our microwave is an older stainless steel model from about eight years ago.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A slight degradation in the microwave door seal allows trace RF leakage, overwhelming WiFi channel 6 and causing immediate packet loss.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes complete sense! How do we prevent it from knocking out my laptop?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We will log into your S-Net Hub manager, shift your 2.4GHz frequency to channel 11 away from the microwave emission peak, and establish a dedicated 5GHz network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How do I access the Hub manager from my laptop?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open your web browser and type: 192.168.1.254 into the address bar, then press Enter.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Typing 192.168.1.254... the S-Net Smart Hub home page has loaded asking for the Admin Password.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The admin password is the eight-character code printed on the pull-out plastic card behind the hub.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Got the card... typing: K7M2P9X4... logging in now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click on Advanced Settings, then select Wireless.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Advanced Settings... Wireless. I see two sections: 2.4 GHz Configuration and 5 GHz Configuration.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under 2.4 GHz, change Channel Selection from 'Auto' to 'Channel 11', which sits furthest away from 2.45 GHz microwave noise.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Selected Channel 11. What about the 5 GHz band?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under 5 GHz, toggle 'Separate SSID' to ON, and add '-5G' to the end of your wireless network name.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Toggling Separate SSID to ON... network name is now 'SNet-Fletcher-5G'. Clicking Save.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The hub is applying the dual-band configuration. 5 GHz operates on an entirely separate radio spectrum that is completely immune to microwave interference.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The hub light blinked amber and has returned to solid blue.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On your laptop, connect directly to the new 'SNet-Fletcher-5G' network using your existing WiFi password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Entering password on laptop... connected to SNet-Fletcher-5G with full signal bars!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let us perform a real-world test. Please have someone turn on the kitchen microwave for one full minute while we monitor connection stability.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm calling into the kitchen... my son is running the microwave with a mug of water for sixty seconds. Microwave is humming right now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am sending a continuous ICMP packet ping stream to your laptop's IP address.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The microwave just beeped and finished. The WiFi icon never blinked once! My web page stayed completely responsive!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Zero dropped packets across sixty seconds of continuous microwave operation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What a tremendous difference! 5G is totally unaffected!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously that confirms the microwave leakage was strictly confined to the 2.4 gigahertz spectrum band, Wendy.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That completely solves the dropouts for my NHS work station.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have you tried swapping the ADSL microfilter on your telephone wall socket to see if that helps with the signal?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Dominic, I explained at the very start of our phone call that I replaced the microfilter yesterday with a brand new S-Net filter! Didn't you hear me say that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I apologize, Wendy, you did indeed mention replacing the microfilter earlier. My mistake.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Alright, as long as we know the 5GHz frequency solved the microwave problem.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to check, Wendy, is your landline telephone working clearly without any crackle or static noise?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, our landline dial tone is completely clear and quiet.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also check your Ethernet network adapter settings in case you ever want a wired backup cable directly into the hub.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I do have a yellow Ethernet cable in the box that came with the router. Would that give an even faster connection?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: An Ethernet cable provides a direct gigabit physical connection that cannot be disrupted by any household appliances whatsoever.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will keep that cable plugged into my desk dock for days when I have extra heavy transcription workloads.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will remain the dedicated owner for this support case and note the 5GHz separation on your customer file.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Dominic, that gives me enormous relief for submitting my hospital reports this afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Ensure your other family devices such as mobile phones and tablets also connect to the Fletcher-5G network for best speed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will connect our tablets to the 5G network as well.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your S-Net broadband or router configuration that I can assist you with today, Wendy?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that has sorted my connection completely. Thank you Dominic.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You may receive a brief customer satisfaction survey by SMS after this call; we would appreciate any feedback you can share.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will fill out the survey. Have a good afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Wendy. Have a wonderful day and take care.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, goodbye.
